data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Rank-22 decompositions of the <3,3,3> tensor are obstructed by a symmetry-preservation constraint: any rank-22 decomposition must either fix the tensor's full automorphism group action or lie in an orbit that cannot close under the Clebsch-Gordan-style degeneracy present at rank 23. Over GF(2), an exhaustive search over symmetry-restricted rank-22 triples will return empty, while the Laderman rank-23 orbit lifts, discriminating this hypothesis from a 'merely hard to find' hypothesis.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If a symmetry-restricted rank-22 decomposition over GF(2) is found, the obstruction hypothesis is weakened and attention shifts to lifting from GF(2) to Z.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If an unrestricted rank-22 decomposition over GF(2) exists but no symmetry-restricted one does, the obstruction is to symmetry-preserving decompositions specifically, not to rank 22 generally.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the symmetry-restricted search space is larger than estimated (stabilizer is trivial rather than S_3-acting), the search may not complete and the experiment is inconclusive rather than discriminating.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the Laderman rank-23 decomposition does not lift to a symmetry orbit over GF(2), the calibration anchor fails and the comparison is invalid.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The <3,3,3> tensor has automorphism group containing (GL_3)^3 semidirect S_3 (permuting the three legs). Rank-23 Laderman decompositions are known to sit in orbits under this group. For rank 22, the orbit-stabilizer counting over GF(2) becomes infeasible because the stabilizer dimension collapses: a rank-22 triple would need to satisfy 729 polynomial constraints with only 22*27=594 free coefficients, leaving a 22*27 - 729 = -135 dimensional deficit. While negative dimension doesn't prove impossibility (non-generic tensors can have rank far below generic), the specific structure of the matrix multiplication tensor's flattening ranks (each 2-flattening has rank 9) combined with the symmetry requirement forces a rigid system. Over GF(2), an exhaustive backtracking search over coefficient matrices modulo 2, restricted to triples respecting the S_3 leg-permutation symmetry, will either find a rank-22 solution (falsifying the obstruction) or exhaust without one (supporting it). The experiment is exactly decidable and runs in seconds for the symmetry-restricted subspace because it reduces the search from 594 binary variables to roughly 594/6 \u2248 99 effective variables under symmetry projection.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
